summary: The main article describes a photoredox-mediated dearomative functionalization of electron-rich heteroarenes using HAT chemistry. It includes one optimization table and three schemes detailing the reaction scope for various heteroarenes and nucleophiles, as well as mechanistic studies.

items.heading: Scheme 1
items.caption: Reductive dearomatization methods.
items.description: Comparison of traditional Birch reduction methods with the newly developed photoredox-enabled dearomative functionalization strategy.

items.heading: Table 1
items.caption: Reaction condition optimization
items.description: Optimization of photocatalysts, HAT agents, and solvents for the dearomative ring-cleavage of 2-methoxythiophene with pyrazole.

items.heading: Scheme 2
items.caption: Scope of heteroarenes.
items.description: Substrate scope for the dearomatization of various thiophenes, furans, benzothiophenes, and indoles.

items.heading: Scheme 3
items.caption: Scope of nucleophiles.
items.description: Exploration of different nucleophiles including azoles, amines, acids, alcohols, and phosphites in the dearomatization process.

items.heading: Scheme 4
items.caption: Proposed mechanism and designed experiments for mechanistic studies.
items.description: Detailed mechanistic pathway involving SET oxidation and HAT, supported by competition and deuteration experiments.
